paragraphs.text: Two runes, merged into one symbol.

Start with the detail itself. The Bluetooth logo is a Viking king's initials. Two runes, merged into one symbol. The name honours King Harald Bluetooth, who united Denmark and Norway. At an industry meeting, Intel's Jim Kardach suggested it as a temporary code name. Harald united Scandinavia. This radio link would unite PCs and phones. It was only a placeholder. RadioWire or PAN was meant to replace it. PAN was already everywhere online, and RadioWire's trademark check ran out of time. So the logo merges Harald's initials in runes: H and B.

Its history begins with a practical problem. King Harald Bluetooth Gormsson was known for uniting Denmark and Norway in 958. Harald's nickname came from a dead tooth of a dark blue-grey colour. In 1996 Intel, Ericsson and Nokia met to plan the standardization of a short-range radio technology. At that meeting Jim Kardach of Intel suggested Bluetooth as a temporary code name. Kardach proposed the code name after seeing a picture of Harald Bluetooth's runestone in a history of the Vikings.
That problem shaped the design. PAN already had tens of thousands of hits on the internet. A full trademark search on RadioWire could not be completed in time for launch.

The documentation makes the purpose clearer. The governing physics: The logo is a bind rune that merges the Younger Futhark runes for Harald Bluetooth's initials. Kardach compared Harald uniting Scandinavia with uniting the PC and cellular industries through a short-range wireless link.

But one detail complicates the familiar story. Bluetooth sounds like a technical acronym, but it is a king's nickname that was meant to be a placeholder. Bluetooth was intended only as a placeholder name. The planned replacement names were RadioWire or PAN (Personal Area Networking).
The design did not stop changing there. A temporary code name became the permanent name and logo of a global wireless standard.
Now the opening question has a precise answer. The Bluetooth logo is a bind rune merging the Younger Futhark runes Hagall and Bjarkan, Harald's initials.
